title: How do we simplify powers that are multiplied?
description: Five multiplications of powers are simplified, including a negative exponent, a letter base and a letter exponent. Keeko doubts whether the exponents are added or multiplied.
teaching_notes: One idea: when powers of one base are multiplied, the exponents are added, even when an exponent is negative or a letter. Watch for students who multiply the exponents, or who forget to change a different base to the common base.

source: Simplify: 2 to the power −4 × 2 to the power 7; 3² × 3 to the power −5 × 3 to the power 6; p³ × p to the power −10; 2⁴ × (−4) to the power −2; 8 to the power p × 8 to the power q.
video_script.why: A learner sees that adding the exponents works for negative and letter exponents, and that a different base is first changed to the common base.
video_script.substitution: the book's own five multiplications of powers
video_script.anchor: five multiplications of powers written in a column on the board
video_script.wrong_answer: two to the power negative twenty eight
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the exponents negative four and seven instead of adding them
video_script.payoff_line: With the same base, we add the exponents, even when they are negative

final_answer.value: 2³, 3³, p to the power −7, 1, and 8 to the power p + q
final_answer.spoken: two cubed, three cubed, pee to the power negative seven, one, and eight to the power pee plus queue

maths_rules: n^a x n^b = n^(a + b), n is not 0
video_script.design: One idea: same base, add the exponents. Wrong idea: multiply the exponents. Each multiplication is solved on its own line; the letter power with a negative exponent only appears at the answer, and a number check shows why the exponents are added.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; five multiplications of powers in a column with a question mark

marks.one: 2^-4 x 2^7 is written in the column
marks.two: 3^2 x 3^-5 x 3^6 is written in the column
marks.three: p^3 x p^-10 is written in the column
marks.four: 2^4 x (−4)^-2 is written in the column
marks.five: 8^p x 8^q is written in the column
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the column

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Simplify two to the power negative four times two to the power seven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Then three squared times three to the power negative five times three to the power six.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Then pee cubed times pee to the power negative ten.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Then two to the power four times negative four in brackets, to the power negative two.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The last is eight to the power pee times eight to the power queue.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we simplify each one?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 2^3 x 2^2 = (2 x 2 x 2) x (2 x 2) = 2^5; the exponents 3 and 2 are added

marks.three: three 2s are drawn in a row for 2^3
marks.two: two more 2s are drawn after them for 2^2
marks.all: all five 2s are joined and written as 2^5, with 3 + 2 = 5 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Two cubed is three twos in a row.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two squared is two more twos.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Together there are five twos, and three plus two is five, so the exponents are added.

marks.given: the five multiplications are written in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five multiplications of powers.

beats.on_screen: To find: each one as a single power or number

marks.find: the words each one as a single power or number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each one as a single power, or as a number.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, the bases are the same, so we add the exponents. Negative four plus seven is three, so the first is two cubed.
<bookmark mark='second'/>In the second, two plus negative five plus six is three. That gives three cubed.

marks.rule: p^3 x p^-10 = p^(3 + (-10)) is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, the same rule works with a letter as the base.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Three plus negative ten is negative seven. That is the new exponent of pee.

marks.diff: the bases 2 and -4 are circled as different

narration: <bookmark mark='diff'/>Step three, here the bases are different, two and negative four.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Negative four in brackets, to the power negative two, is one over negative four squared. That is one over sixteen.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Two to the power four is sixteen, and sixteen times one sixteenth is one. One is two to the power zero.

marks.sum: p + q is circled as the new exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, here the exponents are letters, and the base eight is the same.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>We add the exponents, so the new exponent is pee plus queue.

marks.pay: the added exponents are boxed in all five lines
marks.ans: 2^3, 3^3 and p^-7 are written in a row
marks.last: 1 and 8^(p + q) are added to the row

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>With the same base, we add the exponents, even when they are negative.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The results are two cubed, three cubed, and pee to the power negative seven.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Then one, and eight to the power pee plus queue.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 2^-4 x 2^7 = 2^-28, struck out; 1/16 x 128 = 8 = 2^3 beside it
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the first answer is two to the power negative twenty eight. Keeko multiplied negative four by seven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But two to the power negative four is one sixteenth.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Two to the power seven is one hundred and twenty eight. One sixteenth of that is eight.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Eight is two cubed. The exponents are added, not multiplied.
